---
title: "9. Sensitivity analyses"
format: html
---

This script runs the sensitivity analyses the paper reports: a lower viral load threshold after 2008, a propensity model that adds psychiatry visits, and excluding patients who may have filled their prescriptions elsewhere.

::: {.Rcode title="Source code"}
The full R script is available at:

-   [`R/09_sensitivity.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/R/09_sensitivity.R)

This R script file is itself reliant on the following helper files:

-   [`R/setup.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/R/setup.R)
-   [`R/functions.R`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/R/functions.R)

Translated from [`stata/Do Final Analysis.do`](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Harris-Health-STR/blob/main/stata/Do%20Final%20Analysis.do), lines 174-223.

The code sections below are imported directly from that script when this page is rendered.
:::

```{r}
#| include: false
#| eval: true
#| cache: false
knitr::read_chunk("../R/09_sensitivity.R")
```

## A lower threshold after 2008

The assay changed after 2008, so patients who started later are held to 50 copies/mL. The same daily rule is reused with a threshold that depends on the year ART started, and results are tabulated by start year, as the Stata did one `tab ... if YearofARTInitiation==2008` line at a time.

**Current code:** this "ever suppressed" uses all follow-up, not only year one.

```{r}

#| eval: false
```

## Adding psychiatry visits to the propensity model

`update()` refits the propensity model with one more term.

**Current code:** Final Analysis.do computed the new weights (`IPW2`) but its next two models were written with `[pw=IPW]`, the original weights. The R uses the new weights, which is what the paper describes. Anyone comparing with the Stata log should expect these two models to differ.

```{r}
#| label: add-psych-visits-to-propensity
#| eval: false
```

## Possible outside pharmacy

A suppressed viral load measured 90 or more days after the last fill of a drug in the current regimen suggests the patient was getting medication somewhere else. Stata counted days since the last fill with the same running-sum trick used for labs; here the last fill date is filled down and subtracted. A patient is flagged if this happens at any time in follow-up, and the flag is compared between the groups.

```{r}
#| label: flag-possible-outside-pharmacy
#| eval: false
```

## Excluding them

The paper reports that repeating the analysis without these patients gave similar results (data not shown). Final Analysis.do flags the patients but does not contain those models; they were run in a separate scratch file that is not part of this repository. Here the main models are refitted on the published cohort without the flagged patients, unweighted and with the original weights.
